meta.title: Retry idempotent requests with exponential backoff
meta.summary: `request()` now retries failed **idempotent (GET) requests** up to 3 times with exponential backoff. The retry logic lives in a new `retry.ts` module, and an `HttpError` type lets it retry only transient failures (5xx, 429).

strategy.rationale: Start from what callers see (what changed), then go down into the new module (how it works), and finish with the blast radius (existing callers) and tests.

takeaways: GET retries by default; other methods only with `idempotent: true`
`fetchUser` gets retries without any code change; `renameUser` (PATCH) is unaffected
reviewFocus: Are any PATCH/POST callers idempotent and should pass `idempotent: true`?
Does the total backoff (200+400+800 ms) fit within `timeoutMs`?

glossary.definition: A request whose effect is the same no matter how many times it runs, so retrying it is safe.
Waiting base × 2^n between retries to avoid hammering a struggling server.

chapters.title: The big picture
chapters.goal: Get a map of what was added where

scenes.title: Map of the change
scenes.goal: Know the three files' roles and how they relate
scenes.narration: The change has three parts. **client.ts** starts using the new **retry.ts** module, and the policy values come from **config.ts**. The existing caller `service.ts` inherits the new behaviour without any code change.
scenes.question: What does this change add, and where?

scenes.title: request() now wraps send
scenes.goal: The request moved into a send closure that is retried conditionally
scenes.narration: The old request logic moved, unchanged, into a `send` closure. Two things differ: on failure it throws **`HttpError`** instead of `Error`, and the last line wraps the call in `withRetry` **only for idempotent requests**.

steps.text: Unless `idempotent` is set explicitly, **only GET** is retried.

scenes.question: What happens now when a request fails?
scenes.bridge: The map has one entry point, request(), so start there.

scenes.title: Side by side
scenes.goal: Tell moved code apart from new code
scenes.narration: In the split view it is clear the `fetch` block **only changed indentation**. The real changes to review are `HttpError` and the final branch.
scenes.question: Which lines actually changed, and which only moved?
scenes.bridge: The unified diff mixes moved and new code; side by side separates them.

chapters.title: Inside the retry module
chapters.goal: Know when, how often and how long it retries

scenes.title: Into withRetry
scenes.narration: Jump to the definition of `withRetry`. The loop returns as soon as `fn` succeeds. On failure it waits `base × 2^attempt` and tries again **only if the error is transient and retries remain**.

steps.text: 200 → 400 → 800 ms: up to ~1.4 s of extra waiting with 3 retries.

scenes.question: How does the retry loop decide to try again?
scenes.bridge: request() hands failures to withRetry, so follow that call.

scenes.title: What counts as transient
scenes.goal: Know retries are limited to 5xx and 429
scenes.narration: `isTransient` is true only for an `HttpError` with status **5xx or 429**, so client errors such as 404 fail immediately. That check is why `client.ts` now throws `HttpError` instead of a plain `Error`.

steps.text: Keeping `status` around is the reason `HttpError` exists.

scenes.question: Which failures count as worth retrying?
scenes.bridge: The loop only retries transient errors, so what is transient?

scenes.title: Policy lives in config
scenes.narration: The policy values live in `config.retry`; tuning retries in production means changing this one place.
scenes.question: Where are the retry numbers set?
scenes.bridge: The backoff uses policy values; they come from config.

chapters.title: Impact and verification
chapters.goal: Check the effect on existing code and the tests

scenes.title: What about existing callers?
scenes.narration: Find the callers of `request`. `fetchUser` is a GET, so it is **retried automatically**; `renameUser` is a PATCH and behaves **exactly as before**.

steps.text: If this PATCH is idempotent, pass `idempotent: true` to opt in.

scenes.question: Which existing calls are affected?
scenes.bridge: The behaviour is clear; now check who calls request().

scenes.title: What the tests pin down
scenes.goal: Know both core behaviours are covered
scenes.narration: The tests pin down two behaviours: a **503 is retried until it succeeds**, and a **404 fails without retrying**. Note that no test covers the idempotency branch in `request()` itself.
scenes.question: What do the tests guarantee?
scenes.bridge: Finally, check which of these rules the tests pin down.
